verbatim_locators.note: COVERAGE: whole article incl. Tables 1 to 4; supplementary Tables S2 and S3 read as derived text; Tables S1 and S4 DOCX not opened, so supplementary is captions_only and the receipt is partial. No figures exist in the article. ALLELE CONVENTION: this paper treats C as the rs17797882 risk allele (frequency about 0.79); PMID 31145772 treats T (frequency about 0.24) as the risk allele; the two analyses are therefore of opposite alleles of the same SNP, a fact neither paper notes.

entries.proposition: WWOX rs17797882 (risk allele C, risk allele frequency 0.799 in cases and 0.792 in controls): adjusted OR 1.01 (0.91 to 1.12), p 0.7521; no association with type 2 diabetes.
Seven of nine SNPs, WWOX included, are not associated with type 2 diabetes (p 0.05 or above); two are nominal and fail Bonferroni.

entries.proposition: WWOX rs17797882 against HOMA-beta (n 893): effect 0.003, p 0.9064; against HOMA-IR 0.0015, p 0.5941; against fasting glucose 0.002, p 0.5919. No glycaemic-trait association, in contrast to the p 0.014 HOMA-beta coefficient in the Harbin sample read earlier in this lot.
The authors conclude that neither individual SNPs nor the GRS are associated with the glycaemic traits after Bonferroni correction.
entries.snippet: neither the individual SNPs nor the GRS was significantly associated with these quantitative traits

entries.proposition: Power to replicate the original WWOX association is 42 percent (original OR 1.08, risk allele C, frequency 0.792), the lowest of the nine loci.

With controls aged 50 or older the WWOX risk-allele (C) OR is 0.94 unadjusted and 0.95 adjusted, below 1 and opposite to the original 1.08; the Discussion says most SNPs keep the original direction except KCNK16.
